question: q-125485

original_content.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $25{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$ oriented counterclockwise.
original_content.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our curve as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}=1.
$$

The closed curve $C$ is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $1$ and $5,$ respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-1+5 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }4\,\text{d}t \\  & =4t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =4(2\pi )-0 \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $25{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$ oriented counterclockwise. Interpret circulation as the sum of four convergent improper line integrals over the open quadrant arcs, with independent one-sided limits at $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm5)$. The field is undefined at those four points, so the original ordinary circulation is not defined.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The original field is undefined at the four axis intersections, so an ordinary line integral over the whole ellipse is not defined. For the explicit improper interpretation, $r(t)=(\cos t,5\sin t)$ traverses $25x^2+y^2=25$ counterclockwise. On each open quadrant arc,

$$\frac{5}{y}\,dx=\frac{5}{5\sin t}(-\sin t)\,dt=-dt,\qquad\frac{1}{x}\,dy=\frac{1}{\cos t}(5\cos t)\,dt=5dt.$$

Thus the scalar pullback is $4$. Each endpoint has the finite one-sided limit $4$, so each open-arc integral converges absolutely and equals $2\pi$. Their sum is $\Gamma_{\mathrm{imp}}=8\pi$, the unchanged option c. No principal-value cancellation is used, and $F$ remains undefined at the excluded points.

rationale: Supply the omitted convergent improper-integral convention. Four independently convergent quadrant integrals yield 8pi; ordinary original circulation remains undefined.

mathematical_checks.arc_values: Each independent improper integral is 2*pi; sum=8*pi
